claims.text: Creep resistance in FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coatings is governed by coherent interphase dislocation networks.
Interphase dislocation networks nucleate nanoscale twins through non-Schmid deformation in BCC regions.
Dislocation networks and nanoscale twins localized at FCC/BCC boundaries impede dislocation motion and delay progressive plastic deformation.
The starting coating contains discrete, coherent FCC and BCC regions with clean interfaces.
The starting coating has a low density of dislocations and twins.
Below the catastrophic shear-band threshold, deformation will occur primarily through dislocation slip and twin nucleation rather than extensive grain shear or phase collapse.
Non-Schmid effects trigger localized lattice undulations in the relevant operating-stress range.
Coherent FCC/BCC boundaries guide the formation of interfacial dislocation networks and BCC twin boundaries.
Non-Schmid effects in BCC material promote localized dislocation slip.
Constraint from the adjoining FCC phase causes internal elastic stress fields to build up in the BCC phase.
Internal elastic stress fields trigger nanoscale twin nucleation.
Internal elastic stress fields stabilize dislocation networks at FCC/BCC phase boundaries.
The resulting twins and interfacial networks interrupt long-range dislocation motion and thereby resist creep.
A coating with engineered coherent FCC/BCC interfaces will have a slower creep rate than a comparable single-phase coating or dual-phase coating with incoherent interfaces.
A coating with engineered coherent FCC/BCC interfaces will undergo less progressive plastic deformation than the baseline.
After loading, the engineered coating will have a higher density of coherent dislocation networks and nanoscale twins localized at FCC/BCC interfaces than the baseline.
The proposed resistance mechanism remains effective only below the stress that induces widespread shear banding or catastrophic phase instability.
Excessively high stress or temperature can overcome the stabilizing effects of coherent interphase boundaries.
